packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no outside source consulted)

Exposure note: the only non-fragment text I saw is a later ink label on the spine of the host
binding (image-003/004), reading "ABB: PANO[R?] / in / 3: DECRET. LIB" (label of the bound book,
not of the fragment). I did not use it to supply any reading below.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 is an overview of an opened-out limp parchment binding: back cover (left), spine with
  four raised bands, front cover (right), ruler at right edge. The cover is a reused manuscript
  leaf/bifolium, written side outward.
- Back cover (left half): two columns of small, compressed gothic bookhand, c. 75-80 lines per
  column, text upright in the photograph. The first column begins a little below the top edge;
  both columns end c. 4/5 down, leaving a large empty lower margin. No running title seen (top
  edge is abraded/torn). I see no interlinear gloss and no surrounding gloss frame: it looks like
  continuous two-column prose.
- Small coloured paragraph marks inside the columns (green/blue and red traces; e.g. image-010
  line 15, image-006 around lines 4 and 15, image-007 left edge and lower right), and faint red
  strokes in the left margin (image-010, image-014). A darker later-ink word is written between
  lines in the left column (image-002 c. line 6; image-010 c. line 8), probably an interlinear
  correction or catchword-like addition; I cannot read it securely ("...?ma" / "...ndum?").
- Front cover (right half): the same kind of two-column text, but almost wholly rubbed away and
  spotted with dark mould. Only line beginnings by the spine survive (image-004, -008, -012,
  -016). Visible there: a 2-3-line coloured initial, apparently "Q" or "O", red/green
  (image-012, mid-height), a second coloured initial in the outer column (image-013, blue/red,
  round letter), further ghost initials (image-009), a red paragraph mark (image-012 right of
  centre) and a faint red rubric line near the top of the outer column (image-005 bottom left /
  image-009 top left). A later ink mark like "d" or "∂" in the spine-side margin (image-012).
- Tentative interpretation only: a text divided into short sections with coloured initials and
  rubrics on the front-cover side, and dense citation-heavy prose on the back-cover side.

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
Selected: back cover, lower left column (image-010, image-014) and lower right column
(image-011, image-015), which are the only areas where letter-forms resolve. Upper back cover
(image-002, -003, -006, -007) is mostly a blurred offset-like ghost; only isolated words read.
Front cover (image-004, -005, -008, -009, -012, -013, -016, -017): unread, effectively illegible
at this resolution. Raking or UV/multispectral images, or higher-resolution crops of the back
cover, would be needed for a real transcription.

3. TRANSCRIPTION (very low confidence throughout; line numbers counted from top of each image
and approximate because the top lines of each crop are cut)

Back cover, left column, lower part - image-010
image-010 L3:  [illegible] ... ad ei(us)? ... [illegible]
image-010 L4:  [illegible] co(n)tra? ... [illegible] quod? ad
image-010 L5:  [illegible] ad q(ue)? cum ... [illegible]
image-010 L8:  [illegible] ... e. q(ua)l(ite)r? .4. .i.? Quo(modo)? [illegible]   (darker later ink word
               written over/between here)
image-010 L9:  [illegible] ... ergo? ... om(n)e? eor(um)?
image-010 L10: iu(n)cto? diligentes? ... ad consanguineos?
image-010 L11: i(n)terrogat(ur)? e. et c(eter)o? ... [illegible]
image-010 L12: [illegible] ut. p(ro)? [illegible]
image-010 L14: conueniente? et sup(er)? ... [illegible]
image-010 L15: [coloured paraph] Ego? hic casum? ... [illegible, mould stain]
image-010 L16: officio et illum? que? sit ad que? [illegible]
image-010 L17: pedaneo? prout? tunc ... [illegible] in h(oc)? eo
image-010 L18: a quo inquirere? ... [illegible] aliis?
image-010 L19: q(ui)? iudicio? p(ro)pria(m)? non ... [illegible]
image-010 L20: [illegible] p(ro)hibita? ... dicit(ur)?

image-010 L22: in ... ergo? aliunde? ort(um)? [illegible]
image-010 L24: cognita? ... uno modo co(m)mittit(ur)? e. c. ...
image-010 L25: [illegible] etc. eo. ... [coloured paraph] ... [illegible]

image-014 (overlaps image-010 L21-25 at its top; then the last lines of the column)

image-014 L9:  [illegible] non licet? ... [illegible]

Back cover, right column, lower part - image-011

image-011 L13: est illud? ar(gumentum)? q(uod) sit inquisitio d(icitu)r? p(er)? ex...ones?

image-011 L22: [illegible] q(uod) si? ... sic ad alt(er)am? p(ar)te(m)? possit?
image-011 L23: [illegible] sit ex? officio? inquisitione(m)? ... iusta?
image-011 L24: inquisitio? cum e(st)? fama? ... et graues? le-
image-011 L25: [illegible] iudic(is)? inquirere? ... [illegible]

image-015 (overlaps image-011 L22-25 at top; last lines of the column)
image-015 L7:  [illegible] ... p(ro)? ... [illegible]
image-015 L10: [illegible] ... e. p(ro)? c(etera)? et p(er)?
image-015 L11: [illegible] ... et? ... ad?... [last line of column]

Isolated words elsewhere (back cover upper part): image-006 c. L9 "...ac figuris? p..." ;
image-006 c. L13 "p(ri)mus? ... causis? ..."; image-007 c. L12 "...ut eo q(uod)? ... et ... si
... ar. ..." ; image-007 c. L19 "Cartoria? ... monasterii? in eccl(es)ia? sua?" (very doubtful).

4. LIMITATIONS
- The ink is rubbed to a ghost over most of the cover; many "readings" above are word-shapes
  rather than letter-by-letter readings and should be treated as unverified. The recurring word
  I am most confident of is "inquisitio"/"inquirere" in the right column of the back cover, with
  "ex officio" and strings of short sigla (".p.", ".i.", "e.", "c.", "ar.") that look like
  abbreviated citations.
- Line numbers are approximate; crops overlap (image-010/014, image-011/015, 006/010, 007/011).
- Column order across the two covers, and which side of the original leaf this is, cannot be
  determined from these images. Front-cover text not read.
- I could not reach the 15-25 consecutive securely read lines requested; the script does not
  allow it at this resolution.
